questions.solution:
The NOR output is [latex]f=\overline{\overline{AB}E+EF+\overline{C+D}\,F}[/latex]. By De Morgan:
[latex]f=(AB+\bar E)(\bar E+\bar F)(C+D+\bar F)[/latex]

Combine the first two factors: [latex](\bar E+AB)(\bar E+\bar F)=\bar E+AB\bar F[/latex].

[latex]f=(\bar E+AB\bar F)(C+D+\bar F)[/latex]

Answer: [latex](\bar E+AB\bar F)(C+D+\bar F)[/latex]

questions.text:
The following circuit compares two 2-bit binary numbers, X and Y represented by [latex]X_{1}X_{0}[/latex] and [latex]Y_{1}Y_{0}[/latex] respectively. ([latex]X_{0}[/latex] and [latex]Y_{0}[/latex] represent Least Significant Bits)

Under what conditions Z will be 1?
questions.solution:
From the circuit: [latex]Z=X_1\bar Y_1+(X_1\odot Y_1)\,X_0\bar Y_0[/latex].
- First term: the high bits decide, [latex]X_1=1,\ Y_1=0[/latex].
- Second term: high bits are equal and the low bits decide, [latex]X_0=1,\ Y_0=0[/latex].

This is exactly X [latex]\gt[/latex] Y.

Answer: X [latex]\gt[/latex] Y

questions.text: If ABCD is a 4-bit binary number, then what is the code generated by the following circuit?
questions.solution:
Outputs: W = A, X = A [latex]\oplus[/latex] B, Y = B [latex]\oplus[/latex] C, Z = C [latex]\oplus[/latex] D.

Keeping the MSB and XORing each pair of neighbouring bits is the binary-to-Gray code converter.

Answer: Gray code

questions.text: Minimum number of NAND gates required to implement the following binary equation[latex]Y=(\bar{A}+\bar{B})(C+D)[/latex]
questions.solution:
[latex]Y=(\bar A+\bar B)(C+D)=\overline{AB}\cdot\overline{\bar C\bar D}[/latex] (complemented inputs available):
1. [latex]G_1=NAND(A,B)=\overline{AB}[/latex]
2. [latex]G_2=NAND(\bar C,\bar D)=C+D[/latex]
3. [latex]G_3=NAND(G_1,G_2)=\bar Y[/latex]
4. [latex]Y=NAND(G_3,G_3)[/latex]

Answer: 4

Select lines: [latex]S_0=A[/latex], [latex]S_1=B[/latex]. Inputs: [latex]I_0=C,\ I_1=\bar C,\ I_2=\bar C,\ I_3=C[/latex].

Y = C when A = B, and [latex]\bar C[/latex] when [latex]A\ne B[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]Y=A\oplus B\oplus C[/latex].

This is both the sum of a full adder and the difference of a full subtractor (both are the 3-input XOR).
